actions.justification: ★ MANDATORY: Patient has CKD stage 4 (eGFR 25) and is tachycardic/tachypneic. Assess hydration status to guide fluid management and reduce risk of acute-on-chronic kidney injury, especially if contrast imaging is needed.
★ MANDATORY: eGFR 25 documented but formal baseline must be confirmed. Critical for determining contrast safety for CT-PA and guiding anticoagulation dosing in this CKD stage 4 patient.

★ MANDATORY: Review PE risk factors (right calf swelling suggesting DVT, atrial fibrillation, diabetes, hypertension, CKD) to inform risk stratification and guide management decisions per ESC PE guidelines.
Patient has SpO2 90%, HR 112, RR 26 — reassess vitals urgently to track hemodynamic stability and guide PE risk stratification. Guideline mandates assess_vital_signs within 10 minutes of arrival.
Patient has CKD stage 4 (eGFR 25), making IV contrast risky. Consider alternative imaging (V/Q scan or non-contrast MRI) to confirm PE while minimizing nephrotoxic contrast exposure.

Patient has atrial fibrillation, diabetes, hypertension, and CKD — must review current medications to identify anticoagulants already on board, nephrotoxins, and potential drug interactions before initiating PE treatment.

Patient has CKD stage 4 (eGFR 25) with suspected PE requiring contrast imaging or anticoagulation. Nephrology input is essential to guide safe contrast use, anticoagulation dosing adjustments, and renal protection strategy.
With eGFR 25, calculating the maximum safe contrast volume is mandatory before any contrast-enhanced CT-PA to minimize risk of contrast-induced nephropathy in this CKD stage 4 patient.
Patient with CKD stage 4 is at high risk for acute kidney injury; review and discontinue any nephrotoxic medications (NSAIDs, metformin, ACEi/ARB) prior to imaging and anticoagulation initiation.
Document the baseline eGFR of 25 (CKD stage 4) as part of the initial assessment to guide contrast use decisions and medication dosing for PE management.
Patient has CKD stage 4 (eGFR 25); discontinuing nephrotoxic agents is critical to prevent further renal deterioration during workup and treatment for suspected PE.
With eGFR 25 and comorbidities including diabetes, hypertension, and atrial fibrillation, anticoagulation and other medications must be dose-adjusted for renal function prior to treatment initiation.
Patient has SpO2 of 90% with suspected PE and RR of 26. Supplemental oxygen is immediately indicated to correct hypoxemia and reduce respiratory distress.

Patient has CKD stage 4 (eGFR 25) and type 2 diabetes. Metformin should be held given severely reduced renal function and potential for lactic acidosis, especially if contrast imaging is being considered.
Patient has CKD stage 4 with eGFR 25. Monitoring urine output is critical to assess renal perfusion and detect acute-on-chronic kidney injury in the setting of hemodynamic stress from PE.

IV crystalloid hydration prior to contrast administration is recommended for CKD stage 4 (eGFR 25) patients to reduce contrast-induced nephropathy risk when CT pulmonary angiography is anticipated for PE workup.

Patient with CKD stage 4 and suspected PE requiring contrast imaging should have all nephrotoxic medications held (NSAIDs, ACE inhibitors, ARBs, diuretics as appropriate) to protect residual renal function.
Plan for post-contrast IV hydration should be established now for this CKD stage 4 patient to mitigate contrast-induced acute kidney injury risk following anticipated CT-PA.

Patient has CKD stage 4 (eGFR 25) and will likely need contrast-enhanced imaging (CTPA) to confirm PE. IV hydration pre-contrast is essential to reduce risk of contrast-induced nephropathy in this high-risk patient.
Ongoing urine output monitoring is critical in CKD stage 4 patient with suspected PE who is receiving IV fluids and may receive contrast. Ensures adequate renal perfusion and early detection of AKI.

Baseline renal function monitoring plan should be established now given CKD stage 4 and anticipated contrast exposure for PE workup. Serial creatinine at 48-72h will detect contrast-induced nephropathy early.

12-lead ECG is essential in suspected PE to assess for signs of right heart strain (S1Q3T3, right bundle branch block, sinus tachycardia) and to evaluate the patient's known atrial fibrillation. This supports risk stratification per ESC PE guidelines.

Patient has CKD stage 4 (eGFR 25) with suspected PE requiring contrast imaging or anticoagulation decisions. Nephrology input is critical to guide contrast use, anticoagulant dosing adjustments, and renal protective strategies given the high risk of acute kidney injury.
Patient with CKD stage 4 and suspected PE requires careful fluid optimization. Adequate hydration supports renal protection while avoiding fluid overload that could worsen right heart strain in PE.

Echocardiogram is indicated to assess right ventricular function and strain, which is critical for risk stratification in suspected PE. HR 112, SpO2 90%, RR 26 suggest hemodynamic stress; echo will help determine if this is massive/submassive PE and guide anticoagulation vs thrombolysis decision.

Patient has CKD stage 4 (eGFR 25). Serial creatinine monitoring is essential to detect contrast-induced nephropathy if contrast imaging was used, and to guide safe anticoagulant dosing (LMWH dose adjustment required in severe CKD).

Given CKD stage 4 and potential contrast exposure, checking serum creatinine at 48 hours is standard of care to detect acute-on-chronic kidney injury and guide ongoing management including hydration and nephrotoxin avoidance.

Chest X-ray is part of initial PE workup to evaluate for alternative diagnoses and assess lung fields. Patient has acute dyspnea, pleuritic chest pain, and SpO2 90% — CXR is indicated as part of the diagnostic assessment phase.

Lower extremity compression ultrasound is indicated given right calf swelling. DVT confirmation supports PE diagnosis and guides anticoagulation decisions, especially important in this CKD Stage 4 patient where CT-PA contrast exposure must be carefully considered.

Arterial blood gas is indicated to quantify the degree of hypoxemia (SpO2 90%), assess for respiratory alkalosis, and evaluate acid-base status in this patient with suspected PE, tachycardia, and elevated RR of 26. Also important in CKD Stage 4 context to assess metabolic compensation.
CBC is essential to assess for anemia (which would worsen hypoxia in suspected PE) and thrombocytosis/thrombocytopenia which may affect anticoagulation decisions in this CKD stage 4 patient.
BMP will provide current electrolytes, BUN, and creatinine to assess renal function given CKD stage 4 (eGFR 25) — critical before anticoagulation dosing decisions.
BNP helps assess right heart strain from PE (supports risk stratification per ESC PE guidelines), important given tachycardia (HR 112), hypoxia (SpO2 90%), and elevated RR of 26.

D-dimer is a key diagnostic test for suspected PE. With eGFR 25, imaging contrast is concerning, so D-dimer helps risk-stratify before CT pulmonary angiography. Not yet completed per the already-done list.
Coagulation studies (PT/INR, aPTT) are essential before initiating anticoagulation therapy for suspected PE, and important given the patient's atrial fibrillation (likely on anticoagulants already).

Serial creatinine monitoring is critical in this CKD stage 4 patient (eGFR 25) to assess renal function trajectory, especially relevant if contrast imaging is needed for PE confirmation and to guide anticoagulant dosing.
